[core] Deprecate BlackBox in favor of ExtModule (#5103)

Deprecate BlackBox and tell users to switch to ExtModule.  BlackBox has a
ton of baggage associated with it, due to it mandating, at runtime, a
single `val io` call and no additional calls to `IO` while also magically
removing the `io_` prefix in the generated FIRRTL.  `ExtModule` is far
cleaner and works as a user would expect.  You can call `IO` as much as
you want.  No magic prefixing happens.

This is slightly unfortunate as one could argue that `BlackBox` is a good
name.  However, you can also argue (more strongly I would add) that this
is an "external module" and it would be better to call it as such.  If
this is controversial, we can consider a migration back from `ExtModule`
to `BlackBox`.

Migrate some tests that were only testing blackboxes to be duplicated in
the external module tests.  This will allow us to just delete this test
later.

This has three motivations:

1. `BlackBox` has always been janky for the reasons above and `ExtModule`
is the saner generator API.

2. It's bad to have two similar, though subtly different ways of doing
things.

3. The singular IO that `BlackBox` forces users to go through means that
`BlackBox` cannot have domain information attached to it.  This
essentially means that `BlackBox` will be essentially unusable until
domains gain support for being in subfields.  It's easier to just
deprecate `BlackBox` than to require that domains gain this complicated
feature addition just now.

Add mill command to test modules marked as UnitTest (#5163)

Add a `chisel[].unitTest` command that:

1.  Runs the `chisel3.UnitTests` main to discover and build all modules
    marked with the `chisel3.test.UnitTest` trait.
2.  Compiles the generated FIRRTL to MLIR with `firtool`.
3.  Executes the tests in the MLIR file with `circt-test`.

This is a first step towards allowing Chisel to use its own unit test
discovery mechanism, analogous to how ScalaTest works. The main
difference is that the unit tests are just regular Chisel modules, which
together with the `SimulationTest` and `FormalTest` markers can be
compiled into a FIRRTL and MLIR file and later executed with
`circt-test` or any other build system.

As a concrete example, add an exhaustive unit test for the GrayCode
utility.

Allow ChiselSim to link in prebuilt software libraries (#5189)

Add the `libraries` and `libraryPaths` settings to ChiselSim's
`Settings` class that can be passed to `simulate(...)`. These settings
allow the user to provide a list of library names or paths that the
simulator backend should link into the simulator. I envision this to be
used for DPI-based tests to link in implementations for DPI functions.
The build system can use the `CHISELSIM_LIBS` environment variable or
the `chiselsim.libraries` Java property to provide a list of library
names and their paths which the user can call out in `libraries`. This
allows the Chisel code to not hardcode filesystem paths that are likely
to be a build system concern, and instead only call out libraries by
name.

This commit also adds a small C compiler invocation to `build.mill` in
order to build a handful of shared libraries that the simulator unit
tests will use to check the library linking behavior.

Fix memory corruption in svsim (#5203)

There are three places in svsim where the simulation driver allocates a
few bytes of memory to pass a value to a port setter or getter. The code
rounds the number of bits up to the next byte to determine how many
bytes to allocate. The setters and getters however expect an array of
`svBitVecVal`s, which are typedef'd to be `int32_t`s. This leads to
out-of-bounds memory accesses and potentially memory corruption since
the getters expect a memory region sized to accommodate the number of
bits of the port rounded up to the next four bytes.

The fix is pretty straightforward: always allocate a multiple of 4 bytes
to accommodate the `int32_t` array.

[debug] add DebugMeta model, annotation, and constructor param reflection

CtorParamExtractor walks a module's or Bundle's primary constructor via
Java/Scala reflection and serialises its parameters as JSON ClassParam
records.  Booleans round-trip as native JSON bools; numeric types are
serialised as strings to avoid precision loss on Long > 2^53 and the
absence of NaN/Infinity literals.  Nested user-defined objects are
recursed up to a fixed depth; JDK and Scala stdlib classes are treated
as opaque and printed via toString, capped at 256 characters.
EmitDebugIntrinsicsAnnotation doubles as a HasShellOptions source so
--with-experimental-debug-intrinsics activates the pass from the CLI.

CtorParamsPlatform is split by Scala version: the Scala 2 variant uses
scala.reflect runtime mirror; the Scala 3 variant falls back to Java
reflection because Scala 3 lacks a runtime mirror for primary-constructor
selection, and is restricted to single-constructor classes.

Based on work of @rameloni

[debug] add DebugMetaEmitter, AddDebugIntrinsics phase, and integration tests

Add the circuit-walking emitter and the compilation phase that wire the
debug intrinsic pass into the existing elaboration pipeline.

DebugIntrinsics.generate walks every DefModule/DefClass in the elaborated
Circuit and appends four kinds of secret FIRRTL commands:

  circt_debug_moduleinfo  -- one per module: desiredName + ctor params
  circt_debug_var         -- one per top-level signal, port, or memory
  circt_debug_subfield    -- one per Bundle/Vec element, linked by parent
  circt_debug_enumdef     -- one per ChiselEnum type (emitted once)

Subfield emission recurses depth-first and carries the root signal's
local name as the parent attribute, matching the string equality expected
by CIRCT's CirctDebugVarConverter.  Bidirectional (Analog) signals are
excluded from SSA operands because firrtl.int.generic requires passive
types.  Synthetic _-prefixed names are dropped since they do not survive
to final FIRRTL.

AddDebugIntrinsics is a Phase inserted between Elaborate and Convert.
It is a no-op unless EmitDebugIntrinsicsAnnotation is present; after
consuming the annotation it strips it from the seq to prevent
double-emission on a second pass.

Based on work of @rameloni

Add an alternative property assertion API which takes a `Property[String]`
message.  This builds towards allowing for string interpolation in
property assertion messages.  Due to the limited availability of property
operations, this is relatively limited in power and very verbose.  More
operations (e.g., number to string formatting) and better ergonomics are
planned.

Fix an issue where infix `++` did not work for `Property[String]` because
this would fallback to the list version (which also has the same infix
operator).

Using the new property assert that takes a property string message, build
up a greatly improved assertion message when a rational or synchronous
assertion check fails.  This is intended to assists with debugging when
clock domains are misconfigured during compilation or when running
`domaintool`.
